candidates.title: Yang Ming expands Egypt coverage through DP World slot-sharing deal
candidates.excerpt: Yang Ming Marine Transport will expand its shipping connections within Egypt through a slot-sharing arrangement with DP World Shipping Solutions, covering three services linking the country’s main Mediterranean ports. Under the arrangement, the Taiwanese container carrier will take slots on two intra-Egypt services operated by DP World Shipping Solutions, as well as on the Egyptian section of the operator’s Egypt–Syria–Lebanon service. The EG2 service will run fortnightly, connecting: Damietta – Alexandria (El Dekheila) – Port Said. We do not claim that all goods transported under the F-G classifications are being used to build AI data centres, but that they could conceivably be contributing to it. candidates.title: Hapag-Lloyd raises Far East–Europe freight rates from December
candidates.excerpt: Hapag-Lloyd has announced an increase in its Freight All Kinds (FAK) ocean tariff rates for shipments from the Far East to Europe, effective from 1 December 2026, with the highest published rate reaching US$6,800 per 40-foot container. The revised tariffs will apply to 20-foot and 40-foot dry containers, including high-cube equipment, on sailings with a tariffing date on or after 1 December. The rates will remain in effect until further notice. Under the new tariff structure, shipments from the Far East to Northern Europe will be charged US$3,000 per 20-foot container and US$4,500 per 40-foot dry or high-cube container. For the Western Mediterranean and Adriatic, rates will reach US$5,100 per 20-foot container and US$6,400 per 40-foot container. Higher tariffs will apply to Türkiye, Egypt and the Eastern Mediterranean, at US$5,300 per 20-foot container and US$6,600 per 40-foot container. candidates.title: ZIM withdraws from Arkas–Evergreen Black Sea service
candidates.excerpt: ZIM has ended its slot-chartering arrangement on the GPM/BSX service operated by Arkas and Evergreen, withdrawing from a regional container shipping connection linking Piraeus with ports in the Black Sea. The Israeli carrier previously marketed the service as Black Sea Express (BSX), offering connections between Greece, Georgia, Romania and Bulgaria through capacity chartered on the jointly operated service. The service follows the port rotation: Piraeus – Poti – Constanta – Varna – Piraeus. The withdrawal ends ZIM’s participation in this particular slot-chartering arrangement, although it does not represent the termination of the underlying service operated by Arkas and Evergreen. The route provides connections between the Greek port of Piraeus and three Black Sea gateways, serving cargo flows to and from Georgia, Romania and Bulgaria. No specific effective date for ZIM’s withdrawal or details of alternative arrangements for affected customers have been provided.

candidates.title: MSC to launch new North India–Red Sea container service
candidates.excerpt: MSC is preparing to introduce a new container shipping service connecting India and Pakistan directly with Saudi Arabia, with operations scheduled to begin in late November 2026. According to DynaLiners, the new North India–Red Sea service will deploy container vessels with capacities ranging from approximately 2,500 to 3,000 TEU, linking the Indian port of Mundra and Pakistan’s Port Qasim with Jeddah and King Abdullah Port in Saudi Arabia. The planned port rotation will be: Mundra – Port Qasim – Jeddah – King Abdullah Port – Mundra. The service will establish a direct connection between two major container gateways on the Indian subcontinent and Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea coast, expanding MSC’s regional shipping network. The introduction follows other adjustments to MSC’s Red Sea operations, including the planned expansion of its Zephyr service with calls at Jeddah and King Abdullah Port. candidates.title: Asean Seas Line removes Shekou from China–Philippines service
candidates.excerpt: Asean Seas Line (ASL) has revised the rotation of its China–Philippines SVP service, removing Shenzhen (Shekou) as a regular port of call. According to DynaLiners, the revised service is operated by a single container vessel with a capacity of approximately 1,100 TEU, connecting two Chinese ports with Manila and Subic Bay in the Philippines. The updated port rotation is: Xiamen – Nansha – Manila – Subic Bay – Xiamen. The adjustment reduces the service’s regular Chinese port coverage to Xiamen and Nansha, while retaining its two Philippine destinations. The removal of Shekou represents a further adjustment to ASL’s regional network, following previous changes to its China–Philippines connections. The revised arrangement maintains direct connections between southern China and the Philippine ports of Manila and Subic Bay. The effective date of the change has not been specified.

candidates.title: English region gets behind rail freight development
candidates.excerpt: English region gets behind rail freight development North Lincolnshire Council is commissioning a feasibility study to identify opportunities to increase rail freight movements across its area. The work will examine existing railheads and sidings, potential new sites, network access and the commercial viability of additional rail-based services. It will also assess the wider economic, social and environmental benefits of developing rail freight infrastructure. The initiative forms part of a broader examination of rail’s contribution to the region’s economic development. Funded through the Greater Lincolnshire Growth Fund, the £72,000 (€86k) study will provide evidence to support future decisions on investment. It will consider whether new or improved infrastructure could strengthen North Lincolnshire’s position as a major freight and logistics hub. US rail traffic hits intermodal record as October freight gains signal economic resilience, says AAR
candidates.excerpt: U.S. railroads set an intermodal traffic record in October as shipments rose across much of the freight economy, evidence of resilient demand despite inflation, higher interest rates and weak consumer confidence. Intermodal volume rose 9.6% from a year earlier, with railroads handling an average of more than 298,000 containers and trailers per week — the highest weekly average for any month on record, according to the Association of American Railroads. Total carloads increased 3.4%, their strongest percentage gain in eight months, while carloads excluding coal climbed 4.5%. Fifteen of the 20 carload categories tracked by the AAR posted year-over-year increases in October, and 16 were higher through the first 10 months of 2026. The association said that breadth pointed to underlying industrial strength rather than simply a shift of freight from highways to rail. candidates.excerpt: TugVolt autonomous wagons to be trialled on Missouri railway USA: Two of Intramotev’s TugVolt battery-powered autonomous wagons are to be trialed on the 35 km Columbia Terminal Railroad, which runs between Centralia and Columbia in Missouri. The Federal Railroad Administration-approved test programme will begin with remote shunting at COLT’s Columbia terminal, and progress to autonomous freight services along the full main line, which includes public crossings. This will produce a safety record that FRA and the more than 600 other US short lines can use as a template for adopting autonomous wagons.
